title: Mila, Pipo, and the Night the Fireflies Went Dark
description: Mila, Pipo, and their friends search for the missing lights and discover how calm voices and company can help courage grow.

cover.alt: Mila and Pipo, at the lower left, look up at a night sky full of fireflies.

illustration.alt: Mila steps out of the house with an empty jar, and Pipo joins her in the garden at sunset.

blocks.title: Into the garden
lines: At six o'clock, Mila steps into the garden carrying an empty glass jar, excited to watch the evening lights beside Pipo.
Above the house, the evening sky is changing from orange to purple as the tree stretches long shadows across their path.
They have watched fireflies here on other evenings, but tonight the silent garden seems to be waiting for something new.
One light, two lights… where are the lights?

illustration.alt: The dark garden, Mila holding the jar, Pipo sniffing the ground, and Tito crying in four panels.

blocks.title: No lights
lines: The garden looks unbelievably dark beneath the tree.
Leaves brush together softly, but no yellow lights appear.
Mila waits and listens to the breeze moving through them.

blocks.title: The empty jar
lines: Mila's jar catches the last faint colors of the sunset.
She holds it toward the bush, but she can't see a firefly.
The familiar garden suddenly feels like a different place.

blocks.title: A little trail
lines: Pipo lowers his nose until it almost touches the damp ground.
He finds a tiny trail winding between the roots.
Perhaps this is where their unexpected adventure will begin.

blocks.title: Tito is crying
lines: Tito pushes through the leaves with tears on his cheeks.
—They’ve all gone dark! —he cries, pointing upward.
His friends move closer, ready to hear what has happened.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, Tito came out with tears on his cheeks.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the last picture on page two and find the tears.

variants.prompt: Who needed comfort when they met in the garden?

options.text: Tito, who was upset about the missing lights.
Mila, who had lost her jar.
Dora, who could not find her book.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, Tito was worried, and his friends listened to him.
variants.retryFeedback: Return to page two and notice who comes out crying.

illustration.alt: Tito points to a cloud covering the moon; Mila and Pipo get ready to help him.

blocks.title: The cloud
lines: —A big cloud covered the moon —Tito explains shakily.
—The fireflies don't like the dark —he continues.
—They were frightened, so they hid their lights —he finishes.

blocks.title: Together
lines: —I want to find them and help —Mila says firmly.
—I'll come too, even if I'm scared —Pipo replies.
Together, they turn toward the path beyond the garden.

illustration.alt: A snapped twig, Pipo in a puddle, an owl, frightened Tito, Pipo sneezing, and the stream.

blocks.title: The twig
lines: Crack!
A dry twig snaps beneath Mila's bright red shoe.
She checks the ground before stepping on.

blocks.title: The puddle
lines: Splash!
Pipo lands in a puddle and splashes his own wings.
He shakes off the drops and keeps going.

blocks.title: The owl
lines: Whoo!
An owl calls from a branch, making the three friends stand still.
It is only a forest neighbor saying hello to the night.

blocks.title: Tito’s heartbeat
lines: Thump, thump!
Tito's heart beats like a little drum.
His paws tremble, but he stays with his friends.

blocks.title: The sneeze
lines: Achoo!
Pipo sneezes loudly and rubs his nose with one paw.
Then he takes another step along the path.

blocks.title: The stream
lines: At last they hear water flowing in the stream.
The bank is still dark beneath them.
One light, two lights… where are the lights?

illustration.alt: The bark bridge over the stream; Tito crosses while Pipo and Mila wait for their turns.

blocks.title: The bark bridge
lines: Their old bark bridge is still resting on its two stones, with the stream rushing underneath.
Mila checks that both ends are supported and reminds her friends to cross one at a time.
Being courageous can mean taking one careful step, then giving someone else the space to take theirs.
They agree to wait on the firm bank.

blocks.title: The first turn
lines: Tito goes first, placing one small paw ahead of the other.
He counts one when he reaches the bank and breathes out.
Then he turns to wait for his friends.

blocks.title: The next turns
lines: Pipo is second, holding his tail up above the water.
Mila is third and counts three as she reaches solid ground.
Everyone has crossed safely by taking a separate turn.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, Tito took the first turn.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the lower left picture on page five.

variants.prompt: In what order did they cross the bridge?
variants.correctFeedback: Exactly: they waited and crossed one at a time.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread the two lower pictures on page five and follow their turns.

illustration.alt: Mila, Pipo, and Tito visit the hollow tree; Dora holds her blue book with a yellow star.

blocks.title: Dora and her book
lines: On top of the hill, they find a hollow tree with a round doorway tucked between its roots.
Dora the stork lives there, and she comes down to meet them with a large blue book.
A yellow star decorates the cover of the book of lights, the treasure she looks after.
She listens closely to Tito, then tells the friends that its pages can show them how to help.

blocks.title: The riddle
lines: Before she opens the book, Dora offers a riddle and asks them to listen to both clues.
—What has leaves but isn't a tree, and tells stories without a mouth? —she asks gently.
Pipo looks up at the branches, though he suspects the answer is not growing there.
Mila repeats the clues to remember them, while Tito moves a little closer to his friends.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, Dora looks after the book of lights.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at what Dora is holding on page six.

variants.prompt: What does Dora keep in the hollow tree on the hill?

options.text: A clear glass jar that she uses to carry water from the stream up to her home.
The book of lights, whose pages show how to help someone who feels frightened.
A box of dry leaves that she puts across the bridge whenever it starts to rain.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, the book holds a way to help others feel less afraid.
variants.retryFeedback: Return to page six: find the star on the cover and reread what Dora brings.

illustration.alt: Lightning crosses the sky; Tito hides behind Mila beneath an empty comic burst shape.

blocks.title: Thunder
lines: Boom! Boom! Boom!

blocks.title: Staying close
lines: Thunder rolls over the hill, and Tito ducks behind Mila.
The sudden noise makes his little paws shake again.
She stays beside him, giving him time to feel steady.

illustration.alt: Mila sits thinking, with a yellow light bulb above her head and a book beside her.

blocks.title: The song
lines: One light, two lights… where are the lights?
Mila hums the song while she sorts the clues in her mind.

blocks.title: The clues
lines: Leaves can grow on branches, but the leaves inside a book are made of paper.
It's a book that can tell a story; a tree cannot do that, though both have leaves.

blocks.title: The answer
lines: —A book! —Mila says, delighted that the two clues fit together.
Dora nods and opens it where everyone can see the pictures.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, she thought about the paper leaves in a book.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread page eight and look for the two kinds of leaves.

variants.prompt: How did Mila work out the answer to the riddle?

options.text: She heard thunder and thought it came from a book cover.
She connected paper leaves with the stories inside a book.
She found a hidden firefly shining inside her empty jar.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, she put the clues together to find an answer that fit.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread Mila’s thoughts on page eight: what has leaves and tells stories?

illustration.alt: An open book, Mila breathing, Dora counting one, two, and three on her fingers, and Mila singing.

blocks.title: The open book
lines: Dora rests the open book across her wings for them to see.
Its pictures show three simple steps to follow.
Now the friends have a way to help.

blocks.title: A deep breath
lines: —Take a slow breath —Dora says in a gentle voice.
They breathe in, pause briefly, and let the air flow out.
Tito notices his paws beginning to feel less tight against the ground.

blocks.title: One
lines: Dora lifts one finger and says one.
Tito watches and copies her.
Everyone takes a quiet moment.

blocks.title: Two
lines: Dora raises two fingers and counts two in a calm voice, leaving a little space after the word.
The friends keep their feet still on the grass.
There is no need to hurry when they can give each other time to breathe.

blocks.title: Three
lines: Dora holds up three fingers and finishes the count with a smile.
Pipo lets his wings relax instead of squeezing them close.
Tito notices that his heart is no longer racing quite so fast.

blocks.title: A quiet song
lines: Mila starts a tune as soft as the breeze in the leaves.
Pipo hums on and on and on, keeping his voice low.
Tito joins in at last.

illustration.alt: Three fireflies in separate columns, each glowing more brightly than the last.

blocks.title: The first light
lines: A firefly blinks on beside a leaf at the edge of the path, casting a tiny circle of light.
It is the first to leave its hiding place, drawn by the soft voices of its new friends.
They keep singing where they are, leaving it plenty of room to explore without being chased.

blocks.title: The second light
lines: The second firefly switches on near another leaf, helping illuminate a little more of the path.
Its glow seems to answer the first, as though the two lights are sharing a quiet secret.
Mila holds her open jar toward their reflections, happy to watch without catching them.

blocks.title: The third light
lines: A third firefly shines with an extraordinary golden glow, circling above the dark grass.
Tito counts the three bright lights and feels a smile spreading all across his face.
Some fear is still there, but now he has room for joy beside it, and that feels wonderful.

variants.prompt: How did the first lights appear?
variants.correctFeedback: Yes, they came on one after another.
variants.retryFeedback: Follow the three columns on page ten from left to right.

variants.prompt: What best describes how the lights began to return?

options.text: One firefly came out, and then two more joined it.
All three went dark before the first appeared.
Every firefly in the garden lit up at the same instant.

variants.correctFeedback: Exactly: the light returned a little at a time.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread the three columns on page ten and follow the first, second, and third lights.

illustration.alt: Six lights in the dark sky; three more appear as the cloud drifts away and the friends watch.

blocks.title: Four, five, six
lines: Four, five, six: new lights join the first three fireflies.
The leaves along the path begin to shine softly.
One light, two lights… where are the lights?

blocks.title: Seven, eight, nine
lines: Seven, eight, nine: three more lights rise above the path.
The cloud starts drifting slowly away from the moon.
The friends keep singing as they look up together.

illustration.alt: The sky fills with fireflies as the cloud moves away; Tito laughs happily.

blocks.title: All the lights
lines: —The cloud is leaving, and they're all coming out —says Mila.
—Our quiet song helped them feel less alone —Pipo replies.
—Now I can smile again —Tito says, watching them rise.

blocks.title: Tito’s laugh
lines: —And you helped me when I was frightened too —Tito adds.
He laughs, his cheeks dry and his eyes bright with delight.
Mila and Pipo share his happiness as the lights dance above them.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, the quiet song helped them feel less alone.
variants.retryFeedback: Remember the singing on page nine, then look at the lights on page twelve.

variants.prompt: Why did the fireflies feel ready to come out?

options.text: Tito banged on the tree to wake them up.
Mila shut them inside the jar.
Gentle voices and company helped them feel brave.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, the friends helped by being calm and staying nearby.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread Pipo’s words on page twelve and remember the song.

illustration.alt: Pipo carries the glowing jar, the friends cross the bridge, and Mila looks up at the sky.

blocks.title: A jar of light
lines: Pipo carries the open jar, full of yellow reflections.
The fireflies move freely through the air around them.
Their glow travels with the friends all the way home.

blocks.title: Back across the bridge
lines: They cross the illuminated bark bridge, each at their own pace.
The lights reveal the stones and the water.
This time, everyone can see where to put their feet.

blocks.title: Helping is brave
lines: Mila realizes that being brave does not mean never feeling frightened.
Sometimes it means listening, staying close, and helping a friend try one more step.
As she walks home, she decides that helping Tito has taught her something about herself too.

illustration.alt: The house and garden beneath a night sky full of tiny yellow lights.

blocks.title: The lights at home
lines: The house welcomes them back to a garden full of light, where small gold dots dance among the leaves beside the doorway.
Mila sets the open jar down by the door, happy that nobody needs to shut those little lights inside to enjoy their glow.
Before going in, she looks at the others and remembers that helping someone else find courage made her own grow tonight.
One light, two lights… there are the lights!

options.text: They helped each other feel brave

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, they stayed together and helped one another.
variants.retryFeedback: Think about how Tito felt at the start and how he feels at the end.

variants.prompt: What does this adventure show us about bravery?

options.text: Being brave means never feeling afraid.
Helping someone else find courage is a kind of bravery too.

variants.correctFeedback: Yes, we can feel afraid and still be there for a friend.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread Mila’s thought on page thirteen, then look at the ending on page fourteen.
